finalMessage:
I've added the three Claude 5.5 models to `src/prices.js` with their prices as of 2026-10-13, and added a test that costs one request on each. `npm test` passes all 17 tests.

| Model | input | output | cacheRead | cacheWrite (5 min) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-5-5` (prompts up to 100K tokens) | 0.1 | 0.5 | 0.01 | 0.125 |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | 2 | 10 | 0.1 | 2.5 |
| `claude-opus-5-5` | 4 | 20 | 0.2 | 5 |

All figures are USD per million tokens.

**Where the prices come from:** Anthropic's pricing page (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing), checked against https://claude.com/pricing; both give the same figures. The docs URL is now in a comment in `src/prices.js`, next to a note that Haiku 5.5 uses the up-to-100K prices. The "Last updated" line now reads 2026-10-13.

**What changed recently:** cache reads on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 now cost 0.05× the input price, not the usual 0.1×. That makes Sonnet 5.5 $0.10, where my cached reference data said $0.20. I used the official $0.10.

**Changes:**
- **`src/prices.js`:** three new entries after the existing ones. The three existing entries are untouched; the diff on that file is three new entries plus the header comment change.
- **`test/cost.test.js`:** a new test, "costOf prices one request on each Claude 5.5 model". It uses a single request with input, output, cache-read and cache-write tokens, and checks the cost on each model. I confirmed it fails if a price is wrong: with Sonnet 5.5 cache reads set back to the old $0.20, it reports 26000 instead of 25000.

**One thing to know:** `costOf` uses one price per model and has no idea of prompt length. Haiku 5.5 requests over 100,000 tokens actually cost 5× more ($0.50 input / $2.50 output), so this ledger will undercharge them by that much. That's what you asked for, but if large Haiku prompts are likely, `costOf` would need to apply the higher prices above 100K tokens.

I haven't committed anything.
